fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD "…will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills…" (Micah 4:1). The mountain gets lifted up. That's the picture Micah gives.

Splitting isn't what Micah says here. He says the mountain of the house of the LORD "…will be established as the chief of the mountains…" (Micah 4:1). What he says is that it will be raised above the hills, friend.

Clouds are a nice guess, but Micah doesn't mention any. He says the mountain "…will be raised above the hills, and the peoples will stream to it." (Micah 4:1). Micah's point is the lifting up, and the peoples coming.

Right on the money, baker. The nations say, "He will teach us His ways, so that we may walk in His paths." (Micah 4:2). They want to learn. I respect that, because I'm still learning things in my own bakery.

New land isn't what they say they'll get, baker. They say, "He will teach us His ways, so that we may walk in His paths." (Micah 4:2). They're going up to the mountain to be taught. No moving boxes needed for this trip.

Not quite, baker. The verse says the opposite: "Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor will they train anymore for war." (Micah 4:3). Once the swords are plowshares, nation won't take up the sword against nation. They won't train for war anymore either, friend.

False is right. Micah says, "Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor will they train anymore for war." (Micah 4:3). Nations won't take up the sword against each other, and they won't train for war. That's a whole lot of retired war gear.

You got it, baker. Each man sits under his own vine and fig tree, "…with no one to frighten him." (Micah 4:4). I spent years in the dark listening for the drawer to open, so I know a calm seat is a gift.
Work isn't what Micah says is missing, friend. He says each man will sit under his own vine and fig tree, "…with no one to frighten him." (Micah 4:4). What's missing is anyone to frighten him.

Neighbors aren't what Micah says is missing, baker. The verse says each man sits under his own vine and fig tree, "…with no one to frighten him." (Micah 4:4). What's missing is anyone to frighten him.

The mighty don't show up here, friend. The LORD says, "I will gather the lame; I will assemble the outcast…" (Micah 4:6). He names the lame and the outcast. I'd say that's good news for anyone who's ever felt overlooked.
True, baker. The verse says, "Then the LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from that day and forever." (Micah 4:7). His rule is from that day and forever. That's a ruler worth sticking with.
Careful on this one, friend. Micah 4:7 says, "Then the LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from that day and forever." So the statement is true. His rule is from that day and forever.

Removed would be bad news, baker, and this is good news. The LORD says, "…the former dominion will be restored to you; sovereignty will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem." (Micah 4:8). The dominion is restored to her, and sovereignty comes to her.
